attributes.action: Calculate CMS on net pay after tax/NI, set £100/month minimum & protect overtime
attributes.additional_details:
The current system uses gross income, so working parents are charged on money they never receive after tax and NI. Calculating on take-home pay would be fairer.
The £7 weekly flat rate is too low. A £100 monthly minimum per child would ensure parents take proper responsibility and reduce the burden on taxpayers.
Many parents work overtime just to get by. Including those extra hours discourages extra work. Capping at a 40-hour week would remove this penalty and make the system fairer.
attributes.background: Require the Child Maintenance Service to calculate payments on net income after tax and National Insurance, introduce a minimum of £100 per month per child, and cap assessable income at a standard 40-hour week so overtime is not included.

rejection.details:
We have a lot of petitions open on the Child Maintenance Service:

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions?state=open&q=child+maintenance

Some of them are asking for some for the same things that you are - and you may wish to sign one or more them:

Base CMS payments on NET income not gross
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/778070

Cap income used to calculate Child Maintenance to Minimum Wage over a 40hr week
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/766849

Cap Child Maintenance payments at £200 per child
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/778709

Reduce child maintenance, exclude overtime & introduce no contact, no payment
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/765591

The more petitions we have open on a subject, even when they are asking for different if related things, the fewer signatures they tend to attract as they end up diluting general support.
